title: Ride through the power cut
story: A small logger draws about as much as a 100 Ohm resistor and keeps working down to 3 V. When its 5 V supply disappears, a capacitor charged to 5 V must keep it at 3 V or more for 10 ms so it can save its data. The board has no room for anything bigger than 220 uF. Choose the capacitor.

goals.label: still at least 3 V after 10 ms

hints: The capacitor discharges into the load: v = 5 x e^(-t / RC).
You need e^(-10 ms / RC) to be at least 3/5, so RC must be at least 10 ms / ln(5/3) = 19.6 ms.
With R = 100 Ohm, C must be at least 196 uF. In energy terms, the logger uses 1/2 x C x (5^2 - 3^2) on the way down.
